Thus, \( v(t) < 0 \) when \( 1 < t < 3 \). So, the particle moves in the negative direction during the interval \( (1, 3) \) seconds. Next, calculate the total distance traveled during the first 4 seconds. This requires finding the positions at critical time points (when velocity is zero or at the interval boundaries) and summing the absolute differences in position. Critical points in \( [0, 4] \) are \( t=0 \), \( t=1 \), \( t=3 \), and \( t=4 \). Calculate the position at these times: \( x(0) = 0^3 - 6(0)^2 + 9(0) + 1 = 1 \) \( x(1) = 1^3 - 6(1)^2 + 9(1) + 1 = 1 - 6 + 9 + 1 = 5 \) \( x(3) = 3^3 - 6(3)^2 + 9(3) + 1 = 27 - 54 + 27 + 1 = 1 \) \( x(4) = 4^3 - 6(4)^2 + 9(4) + 1 = 64 - 96 + 36 + 1 = 5 \) Calculate the distance traveled in each interval: Distance from \( t=0 \) to \( t=1 \): \( |x(1) - x(0)| = |5 - 1| = 4 \) units.
